themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked to 8 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 400% surge—suggesting either a pest outbreak, wildlife management failure, or sanitation breakdown in CD108.
evidence: 8 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (400% spike, z-score: 5.74)
Spike is statistically significant and emerged suddenly in the current week
No prior escalation pattern; suggests acute event rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks and DSNY to determine if there's a documented wildlife or pest event triggering complaints
Interview residents in areas with multiple complaints to document health/odor impacts and timeline of sightings

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints rose to 21 THIS WEEK compared to an 11.2 weekly average over 8 weeks—an 87% jump—indicating either increased illegal parking, traffic violations, or service quality issues from Uber/Lyft and similar services.
evidence: 21 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 11.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (87% increase, z-score: 4.28)
Spike emerged suddenly in current week
Aligns with overall high illegal parking volume (1,596 complaints over 90 days) in the district
reporting_angles: Request 311 complaint detail to determine if surge is concentrated geographically (e.g., near transit hubs, shopping districts) or service-specific
Interview TLC and rideshare operators on any service expansions or surge pricing events that may have altered driver behavior this week

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Damage & Disappearance
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints (damaged and missing combined) spiked to 15 over the last 2 weeks versus a baseline of 2.3 weekly average—a combined 550% surge—pointing to possible vandalism, construction damage, or weather events affecting wayfinding and traffic safety.
evidence: Street Sign - Damaged: 9 complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 6.21)
Street Sign - Missing: 6 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.2 weekly average (380% spike, z-score: 3.96)
Combined 15 complaints over 2 weeks; both signals indicate systemic issue with street infrastructure
reporting_angles: Check DOT work orders and construction permits (1,836 filed in last 90 days, mostly alterations) to see if active projects are causing sign damage
Photograph affected areas and map complaint clusters to identify whether damage is concentrated near construction zones or dispersed across the district

themes_detail.label: Helicopter Noise Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Helicopter noise complaints reached 11 three weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 4,300% spike—the highest z-score anomaly in the dataset, suggesting either new flight patterns, military/police operations, or emergency events concentrated in the Upper East Side.
evidence: 11 helicopter noise complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (4,300% spike, z-score: 24.83—highest anomaly in dataset)
Spike is temporally concentrated and has not recurred at the same intensity in subsequent weeks
Residual noise complaints remain elevated but subside, suggesting event-driven rather than structural pattern
reporting_angles: Request FAA flight data and NYPD/FDNY helicopter logs for the week of the spike to identify what triggered the surge
Interview residents affected during the spike week to document noise impact and whether they can recall what event (search operation, medical emergency, etc.) may have caused elevated air traffic

themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints rose to 7 three weeks ago versus a 2.0 weekly average—a 250% spike—warranting investigation into whether a restaurant outbreak, catering event, or food supply contamination affected the district.
evidence: 7 food poisoning complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.0 weekly average (250% spike, z-score: 4.47)
Spike is temporally concentrated; no sustained elevation in following weeks
Upper East Side has high food service density; cluster may indicate common source outbreak
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to request inspection records and violation findings from the week of the spike
Reach out to affected residents (via 311 complaint records if accessible) to identify common restaurants, catering vendors, or food sources
